x: God Almighty means by His saying,
h
The Hour has drawn near

, that the Hour in which the Resurrection will take place has drawn near. His saying, has drawn near, is derived from the verb to be near. This is from God Almighty as a warning to His servants of the approach of the Resurrection and the nearness of the end of this world. He commanded them to prepare for the horrors of the Resurrection before it attacks them while they are heedless and unmindful of it. And His statement,
h
And the moon split
, God Almighty says:
h
And the moon split

, and that was mentioned during the time of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, while he was in Mecca before the migration to Medina. That was because the unbelievers of the people of Mecca asked him for a sign, so he, may God bless him and grant him peace, showed them the splitting of the moon as a sign and proof of the truth of his words and the reality of his prophethood.

But when he showed them, they turned away and denied it and said: This is continuous magic. Muhammad has bewitched us. So God Almighty said: And if they see a sign, they turn away and say, ‘Continuous magic.’ The narrations came in a manner similar to what we said about that, and the people of interpretation said the same.
Mentioning the narrations that were narrated about this and the report of those who said it from the people of interpretation:

c: Bishr told us: Yazid told us: Saeed told us on the authority of Qatada that Anas bin Malik told them that
m: the people of Mecca asked the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, to show them a sign, so he showed them the moon splitting into two parts.
b.via: on the authority of Qatada that Anas bin Malik

c: Ibn Al-Muthanna told us: Muhammad bin Jaafar told us: Shu’bah told us:
m: I heard Qatada narrating on the authority of Anas, who said: The moon split into two parts.

c: Ibn Al-Muthanna and Al-Hasan bin Abi Yahya Al-Maqdisi told us: Abu Dawud told us: Shu’bah told us on the authority of Qatada:
m: I heard Anas say: The moon split during the time of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace.

c: Yaqub Al-Duraqi told me: Abu Dawud told us: Saeed told us on the authority of Qatada:
m: I heard Anas say, and he mentioned something similar.

c: Ali bin Sahl told us: Hajjaj bin Muhammad told us, on the authority of Shu’bah, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Anas, who said:
m: “The moon split twice during the time of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace.”

c: Muhammad bin Abdullah bin Buzaie told me: Bishr bin Al-Mufaddal told us: Saeed bin Abi Aruba told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: on the authority of Anas bin Malik (that the people of Mecca asked the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, to show them a sign, so he showed them the moon in two halves until they saw Hira between them).

c: Abu Al-Sa’ib told me: Mu’awiyah told us, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Ibrahim, on the authority of Abu Mu’ammar, on the authority of Abdullah, who said:
m: “The moon split while we were with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, in Mina, until a portion of it went behind the mountain. Then the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Bear witness.”

c: Ishaq bin Abi Isra’il told me: Al-Nadr bin Shumayl Al-Mazini told us: Shu’bah told us, on the authority of Sulayman, who said:
m: I heard Ibrahim, on the authority of Abu Muammar, on the authority of Abdullah, who said: The moon split into two parts during the time of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. One part was on the mountain and the other part was behind it. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: O God, bear witness.

c: Ishaq bin Abi Israel told us: Al-Nadr told us: Shu’bah told us, on the authority of Sulayman, on the authority of Mujahid, on the authority of Ibn Umar,
m: like the hadith of Ibrahim about the moon.

c: Isa bin Othman Al-Ramli told me: My uncle Yahya bin Isa told me, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Ibrahim, on the authority of a man, on the authority of Abdullah, who said:
m: We were with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, in Mina when the moon split and a group took refuge behind the mountain. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Bear witness.
h
The Hour has drawn near
, and the moon has split.

c: Muhammad bin Amara told me: Amr bin Hammad told us: Asbat told us, on the authority of Samak, on the authority of Ibrahim, on the authority of Al-Aswad, on the authority of Abdullah, who said:
m: I saw the mountain from the opening of the moon when it split.

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya Al-Maqdisi told us: Yahya bin Hammad told us: Abu Awana told us, on the authority of Al-Mughirah, on the authority of Abu Al-Dhaha, on the authority of Masruq, on the authority of Abdullah, who said:
m: The moon split during the time of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. The Quraysh said: This is the magic of Ibn Abi Kabshah, who has bewitched you. So they asked the travelers, and they asked them, and they said: Yes, we have seen it. Then God, the Blessed and Exalted, revealed:
h
The Hour has drawn near
, and the moon has split.

c: Ibn Hamid told us: Jarir told us, on the authority of Mughira, on the authority of Ibrahim, on the authority of Abdullah, who said:
m: The splitting of the moon has occurred.

c: Abu Al-Sa’ib told me: Abu Mu’awiyah told us, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Muslim, on the authority of Masruq, who said:
m: Abdullah had five things that had passed: Smoke, Al-Luzum, Al-Batsha, Al-Qamar, and Al-Rum.

c: Yaqub bin Ibrahim told me: Ibn Ulayyah told us: Ayoub told us on the authority of Muhammad:
m: I was told that Ibn Masoud used to say: The moon has split. He said: Ibn Ulayyah told us:

c: Ata’ bin Al-Sa’ib told us on the authority of Abu Abd Al-Rahman Al-Sulami
m: who said: We stopped in Al-Mada’in and were a farsakh away from it. Then Friday came and my father was with him. Hudhayfah delivered a sermon and said: God says:
h
The Hour has drawn near
and the moon has split. Indeed,
h
the Hour has drawn near

. Indeed, the moon has split. Indeed, the world has announced its parting. Indeed, today is the racetrack and tomorrow is the race. So I said to my father: Will you outpace the people tomorrow? He said: O my son, you are ignorant. Racing is only in deeds. Then another Friday came and we were present and Hudhayfah delivered a sermon and said: Indeed, God the Blessed and Exalted says:
h
The Hour has drawn near
and the moon has split. Indeed,
h
the Hour has drawn near

. Indeed, the moon has split. Indeed, the world has announced its parting. Indeed, today is the racetrack and tomorrow is the race. Indeed, the destination is the Fire, and the one who races is he who races to Paradise.

c: Ibn Al-Muthanna told us: Muhammad bin Jaʿfar told us: Shuʿbah told us, on the authority of ʿAtaʿ bin Al-Saʿib, on the authority of Abu Abd Al-Rahman, who said:
m: I was with my father in Al-Madaʿin. He said: Their leader delivered a sermon - and ʿAtaʿ used to narrate that he was Hudhayfah - and he said regarding this verse:
h
The Hour has drawn near
and the moon has split.
h
The Hour has drawn near
and the moon has split.
h
The Hour has drawn near

and the moon has split. Today is the racecourse, tomorrow is the race, and the one who races will go to Paradise, and the destination will be Hell. I said to my father: Tomorrow is the race. He said: Then tell him.

c: Abu Kurayb told us: Ibn Fadil told us, on the authority of Hisin, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Jubayr ibn Mut’im, on the authority of his father, who said:
m: h
And the moon split
while we were with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, in Mecca.

c: Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Kharijah, on the authority of Al-Hussain bin Abd Al-Rahman, on the authority of Ibn Jubayr, on the authority of his father:
m: h
And the moon split
. He said: It split while we were in Mecca.

c: Muhammad bin Askar told us: Uthman bin Salih and Abdullah bin Abdul Hakam told us: Bakr bin Mudar told us, on the authority of Jaafar bin Rabi’ah, on the authority of Arak, on the authority of Ubaidullah bin Utbah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said:
m: The moon split during the time of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace.

c: Nasr bin Ali told us: Abdul Ala told us: Dawud bin Abi Hind told us, on the authority of Ali bin Abi Talha, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said:
m: The moon split before the migration, or he said that had already happened.

c: Ishaq bin Shaheen told us: Khalid bin Abdullah told us, on the authority of Dawud, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: something similar.

c: Ibn Al-Muthanna told us: Abd Al-A’la told us: Dawud told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, that he said
m: regarding this verse,
h
The Hour has drawn near
, and the moon has split. He said: That had happened before the emigration, and it split until they saw its two halves.

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me: My father told me: My uncle told me: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement,
h
The Hour has drawn near

, and the moon has split… to His statement, continuous magic. He said: It has already happened. The moon had split during the time of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, in Mecca, and the polytheists turned away and said, Continuous magic.

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me: Abu Asim told us: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me: Al-Hasan told us: Warqa’ told us,
m: both on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement,
h
The Hour has drawn near
, and the moon has split, he said: They saw it split.

c: Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Mansur and Laith, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: h
The Hour has drawn near

, and the moon has split. He said: The moon split into two parts, one part remained, and the other part disappeared from the top of the mountain. Then the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Bear witness.

c: Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us,
m: on the authority of

x: And His statement,
h
And if they see a sign

, they turn away. God Almighty says: And if the polytheists see a sign that guides them to the truth of the prophethood of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and evidence that guides them to his truthfulness in what he brought them from their Lord, they turn away from it and turn away, denying it and denying that it is certainly true.
h
And they say

, denying it and denial that it is true: This is magic with which Muhammad bewitched us when it seemed to us that we see the moon split in two by his magic. And it is an ongoing magic. He says: An ongoing magic that will go away, from their saying, This magic has passed away, if it goes away. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me: Abu Asim told us: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me: Al-Hasan told us: Warqa’ told us,
m: both on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, Continuing magic, he said: Going away.

c: Bishr told us: Yazid told us: Saeed told us on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement,
h
And if they see a sign

, they turn away and say, ‘Persistent magic.’ He said: If the people of misguidance see a sign of God’s signs, they say, This is only the work of magic. It is likely that this will continue and then go away.

c: Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us on the authority of Muammar on the authority of Qatada,
m: h
And they say
, ‘Persistent magic.’ He said: Going away.
b.via: Muammar on the authority of Qatada

c: It was narrated on the authority of Al-Hussein,
m: who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubaid told us: I heard Al-Dahhak say regarding His statement,
h
And they say
, ‘Persistent magic,’ as the polytheists say when the moon is eclipsed: This is the work of magicians.

c: Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us on the authority of Sufyan,
m: regarding his statement, Continuous magic. He said: When the moon split into two halves, one halve came from behind the mountain and the other halves went away, the polytheists said when they saw that: Continuous magic.

x: Some of the people of Basra who were knowledgeable in the Arabic language interpreted his saying continuous as meaning that it is a mustaf’il from the verb imrar from their saying: Qad marra al-jabal meaning it became hard, strong, and intense, and amrartuhu ana meaning I twisted it violently. He said: The meaning of his saying
h
And they say continuous magic is intense magic

God Almighty says: And these polytheists from Quraysh denied the signs of God after their truth had come to them and they had witnessed the proof of their correctness by seeing the moon split into two halves. And they followed their desires. He says: And they preferred to follow what their desires called them to of denying that over believing in what they had become certain of the truth of the prophethood of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the truth of what he had brought them from their Lord. And His statement,
h
And every matter is settled

, God Almighty says: Every matter, good or evil, has a settled ending, a settled conclusion, and a settled end. So goodness is settled for its people in Paradise, and evil is settled for its people in Hell.

c: As Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement,
h
And every matter is settled
, meaning that good is for the people of good and evil is for the people of evil.

x: And His statement:
h
And there has certainly come to them of the report that which is a deterrent

. God Almighty says: And there has certainly come to these polytheists of Quraysh who denied the signs of God and followed their whims of report from the previous nations who denied the messengers of God as they are doing, and God brought down upon them of His punishments what is related in this Qur’an that is a deterrent for them. Meaning: And what deters them and restrains them from what they are continuing to do of denying the signs of God, and it is an active participle from the verb to restrain. And in a similar way to what we said about the meaning of that, the people of interpretation said: Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me: Abu Asim told us: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me: Al-Hasan told us: Warqa’ told us,
m: both on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, a deterrent, he said: the end.

c: Bishr told us: Yazid told us: Saeed told us on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement,
h
And there has certainly come to them of the report that which is a deterrent
, meaning this is a Qur’an.

c: Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us on the authority of Sufyan:
m: h
And there has certainly come to them of the report that which is a deterrent
. He said: Deterrent means the end.

x: And his saying, Conclusive wisdom, means by comprehensive wisdom: this Qur’an. And wisdom was raised in response to what in his saying, And there has certainly come to them of the report that in it is a deterrent. The interpretation of the statement: And there has certainly come to them from the report the report of which there is a deterrent of profound wisdom. If the word wisdom had been raised as a resumption, it would have been permissible, and the meaning of the statement would then be: And there has certainly come to them from the report of which there is a deterrent of profound wisdom, or it is profound wisdom, so the wisdom would be like an interpretation of it. His saying,
h
So what use are vows
? There are two interpretations of
h
so what use are vows

: One of them is that it means denial, so if it is directed to that, the meaning of the speech is: So the vows do not use them, nor do they benefit from them, because they turn away from them and deny them. The other is that it means: How, so the meaning of the speech, if it is directed to that, is:
h
So what use are vows
for them? And vow is the plural of vow, like new is the plural of new, and hasr is the plural of mat.

God Almighty means by His saying, Then turn away from them: So turn away, O Muhammad, from these polytheists from your people who, if they see a sign, turn away and say, Continued magic. For on the Day when God’s caller will call to the place of Resurrection, that is the most abhorrent thing.

With their eyes humbled He says: Their eyes humbled, without harm from them. They emerge from the graves which is the plural of grave, which is the graves. The Most High described the eyes with humbleness, not the rest of their bodies. What is meant by this is all of their bodies, because the effect of the humiliation of every humble person and the glory of every honorable person is evident in his eyes, not the rest of his body. Therefore, He singled out the eyes with the description of humbleness. And similar to what we said about the meaning of His statement, with their eyes humbled, the people of interpretation said.
Who said that?

c: Bishr told us: Yazid told us: Saeed told us on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement, with their eyes humbled, meaning their eyes submissive. The reciters differed in his saying with their sights downcast. The majority of the reciters of Medina, some of the Meccans and the Kufians read it as khasha’an with a damma on the kha’ and a shaddah on the sheen, meaning humble. The majority of the reciters of Kufa and some of the Basrans read it as khasha’an absarhum with an alif on the singular, taking into account the recitation of Abdullah. This is because in the recitation of Abdullah it is khasha’an absarhum and they added it, and it is the word of the noun in the singular, since it was an adjective by the rule of a verb, and it does in the singular if it precedes the nouns, as the poet said: And the handsome young men of Ayad bin Nizar bin Ma'ad So, he united the good and it is an attribute of the faces and it is plural and as the other said: The riders throw it into the open spaces, intercepting the necks of its prey and letting it slacken its grip. So it is singular and objecting, and it is a description of necks, and the plural and feminine are permissible in it, as we have explained. And His statement,
h
As if they were locusts spreading out
, God Almighty says: They will emerge from their graves as if, in their spreading out and striving to the place of reckoning, they were locusts spreading out.

x: And his saying,
h
Rushing to the caller

, means: Hastening with their gaze before their caller to that situation. We have explained the meaning of rushing with evidence that makes it unnecessary to repeat it, and we will mention some of what we did not mention in the previous narration.

c: Ibn Hamid told us: Jarir told us, on the authority of Mughira, on the authority of Uthman bin Yasar, on the authority of Tamim bin Hudlam,
m: regarding his statement,
h
Rushing to the caller
, he said: It means rushing.

c: Ibn Hamid told us: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abu Al-Dhaha,
m: h
Rushing to the caller
, he said: rushing. He said: Mahran told us on the authority of Sufyan, Rushing towards the caller. He said: This is how their eyes are fixed on the sky.

c: Bishr told us, Yazid told us, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement,
h
Rushing to the Caller
, meaning intending to go to the Caller.

c: Ali told me: Abu Saleh told us: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement, rushing forward, meaning: looking. And His statement,
h
The disbelievers will say

, ‘This is a difficult day.’ God Almighty says: And the disbelievers in God will say on the Day when the caller will call to something reprehensible: This is a difficult day. They only described it as difficult because of the severity of its terrors and its confusion.

x: This is a threat from God Almighty and a warning to the polytheists of Mecca and all those to whom He sent His Messenger Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, for their denial of him. He has warned them that if they do not repent from their denial of him, he will bring upon them what he brought upon the nations whose stories he related in this surah of destruction and torment. He will save his Prophet Muhammad and the believers in him just as he saved the messengers before him and bought them from the punishment he brought upon their nations. So He, may He be glorified and exalted, said to his Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: You have lied, O Muhammad, before those who denied you from your people who, when they see a sign, turn away and say, Continuous magic, the people of Noah. They denied Our servant Noah when we sent him to them just as the Quraysh denied you when you brought them the truth from us
h
and they said
, He is mad.

And he was warned, which is an active participle from zajarat. And this is what the Arabs do with the letter if it begins with a zay. They make the ta’ of the active participle a dal. From that they say: He was warned from… I rebuked and he declined from Zalfat and I increased from Zadat.
The interpreters differed about the meaning of what they rebuked him for.
Some of them said: Their rebuke of him was that they said: He has gone mad.
Who said that?

c: Ibn Bashar told us: Yahya told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Mansour, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: h
And they said
, ‘He is mad,’ and he was warned. He said: He became crazy.

c: Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: with a similar chain of transmission.

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me: Abu Asim told us: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me: Al-Hasan told us: Warqa’ told us,
m: both on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, and he was deterred, he said: he was driven mad.

c: Ibn Al-Muthanna told us: Muhammad Ibn Jaʿfar told us: Shuʿbah told us, on the authority of Al-Hakam, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding this verse,
h
And they said
, ‘He is mad,’ and he was deterred, he said: He became very mad.

c: Musa bin Abdul Rahman Al-Masruqi told me: Zaid bin Al-Habbab told us: Shu’bah bin Al-Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Al-Hakam, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: something similar.

x: Others said: Rather, their reprimanding him and threatening him with cursing and stoning was with ugly words.
Who said that?

c: Yunus told me: Ibn Wahb told us: Ibn Zayd said
m: about His statement,
h
And they said

, ‘He is mad,’ and he was warned, he said: They accused him, warned him, and threatened him that if he did not do so, he would be among those stoned. And he recited, If you do not desist, O Noah, you will surely be among those stoned Ash-Shu’ara’ 116.

x: And His saying,
h
So he called upon his Lord

, ‘Indeed, I am overcome, so aid.’ God Almighty says: So Noah called upon his Lord, ‘Indeed, my people have overcome me through rebellion and transgression, and I have no power over them. So aid me through a punishment from You for their disbelief in You.’”

God Almighty says, So We opened when Noah called upon Us, seeking help from Us against his people, the gates of heaven with pouring water, which is gushing forth, as Imru’ al-Qais said in describing rain: The morning passed by, then a torrential downpour of rain descended upon it.
The people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us on the authority of Sufyan:
m: with pouring water. He said: It is poured out.

x: And His saying,
h
And We caused springs of water to gush forth from the earth
, God Almighty says:
h
And We caused springs of water to gush forth from the earth

c: Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us on the authority of Sufyan
m: regarding his statement,
h
And We caused springs to gush forth from the earth

, he said: We caused water to gush forth from the earth and it came from the sky. And the waters met for a matter already decreed, he said, mentioning it: So the water from the sky and the water from the earth met for a matter already decreed and ordained by God.

c: Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us on the authority of Sufyan,
m: Then the waters met for a matter that had been predestined. He said: The water of the sky and the water of the earth. It was only said: The waters met for a matter that had been predestined. The meeting does not happen from one person, but rather from two or more, because the water can be a group or one. What is meant by it in this place is: The waters of the sky and the waters of the earth, so the wording of the one was used, but its meaning is a group. It was said: The waters met for a matter that had been predestined, because that was a matter that God had decreed in the Preserved Tablet.

c: Ibn Bashar told us: Muammil told us: Sufyan told us on the authority of Musa bin Ubaidah on the authority of Muhammad bin Ka’b, who said:
m: Food was before bodies and destiny was before calamity. He recited: Then the waters met for a matter already decreed.
b.via: Musa bin Ubaidah on the authority of Muhammad bin Ka’b

x: God Almighty says: And We carried Noah when the water met, on a command that had been predestined, in a ship
h
of planks and nails

. And nails is the plural of dasar. And it is sometimes said for its singular: dasir, just as it is said: habbak and habbak. And dasar is the nail with which the ship is fastened. It is said from it: dasarat al-sailin if you tighten it with nails or something else.
The interpreters differed on this, and some of them said something similar to what we have said.
Who said that?

c: Yunus told me: Ibn Wahb told us: Ibn Zayd told us: Ibn Lahi’ah told me on the authority of Abu Sakhr on the authority of Al-Qurazi,
m: who was asked about this verse:
h
And We carried him on planks and nails
. He said: The nails are the nails.
b.via: Abu Sakhr on the authority of Al-Qurazi

c: Bishr told us: Yazid told us: Saeed told us on the authority of Qatada
m: regarding his statement,
h
And We carried him on planks and nails
. He told us that its nails are the nails with which it was fastened.

c: Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thaur told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement, of planks, he said: the planks of the ship. He said: and nailed: he said: and nailed with nails.

c: Yunus told us: Ibn Wahb told us: Ibn Zayd said

m: regarding his statement, and nails, meaning: nails.

x: Others said: Rather, the stern is the front of the ship. They said: It was described thus because it pushes and pushes the water.

And We carried him on planks and nails

c: Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us on the authority of Muammar on the authority of al-Hasan that he said:

Of planks and nails

Of planks and nails

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me: Abu Asim told us: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me: Al-Hasan told us: Warqa’ told us,

h
It runs before Our eyes
